title: Confirm login-based access and warning behavior before attempting AG/AGV removal actions in Geek
summary: Verify that Geek removal actions (e.g., removing an AGV/AG) are gated by username/password credentials and that initiating a removal action triggers a warning dialog rather than silently proceeding.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm that the Geek application enforces login-based authorization for sensitive removal actions and that the UI provides a warning when a removal is attempted.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the login/role check in Geek and initiate the relevant removal action only far enough to observe whether the warning appears (do not complete the removal if not authorized).
safety_notes: Do not attempt to remove an AGV/AG unless your Geek account is authorized; the source indicates operators do not have the credentials for removal actions.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to initiate the relevant removal action far enough to observe the warning (without completing the action if your role is not authorized)

system_preconditions: Geek application is reachable and you can access the UI for the removal action workflow

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the statement that Geek requires login credentials (operators lack credentials; supervisors have them) and that removal actions come with a warning dialog.

steps.title: Check whether you are logged in with a username/password in Geek
steps.purpose: Confirm that the Geek application is using login-based access (username/password) before testing removal behavior.
steps.instruction: In the Geek application, verify your session is authenticated using a username/password login.
steps.expected_result: You are logged into Geek using a username/password session.
steps.healthy_condition: Geek accepts your credentials and you can access the UI elements needed to attempt a removal action workflow.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot authenticate (no valid login session) or you are not able to access the removal workflow due to lack of credentials.

actions.label: Verify login session
actions.exact_action: Confirm you are logged in with a username/password in the Geek application.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot log in, stop and escalate because you cannot validate warning/authorization behavior.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The application has a username and a password; not everybody has credentials.

steps.title: Verify your role/user has credentials to perform removal actions
steps.purpose: Ensure you are using an account that is authorized for removal actions; the source indicates operators do not have credentials for removal.
steps.instruction: Determine whether your current Geek user role/account is authorized for removal actions (the source indicates operators do not have the credentials; supervisors do).
steps.expected_result: Your account is authorized for removal actions (i.e., you have the credentials expected to perform removal).
steps.healthy_condition: Your account can initiate the removal workflow without being blocked immediately due to missing credentials.
steps.failure_condition: Your account is not authorized for removal actions (e.g., removal initiation is blocked due to lack of credentials).

actions.label: Confirm authorization expectation
actions.exact_action: Use your current Geek login identity/role to confirm you have the credentials expected for removal actions.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you are not authorized (e.g., you are acting like an operator without credentials), stop and escalate; do not proceed with removal testing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Operators don’t have the credentials; supervisors do.

source_evidence.title: Access control for AGV removal actions
source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Operators lack credentials while supervisors do; sensitive actions such as AGV removal are restricted by login-based access.

steps.title: Initiate a removal action and observe whether a warning is shown
steps.purpose: Confirm the UI behavior: removal actions should present a warning dialog rather than silently removing.
steps.instruction: In Geek, initiate the relevant removal action (e.g., removing an AGV/AG) and observe whether a warning dialog appears. Do not complete the removal if your role is not authorized.
steps.expected_result: A warning is shown when the removal action is initiated.
steps.healthy_condition: A warning dialog appears as part of the removal workflow (the source indicates it “will come with a warning”).
steps.failure_condition: Removal proceeds without showing a warning, or the system allows removal without the expected credentials.

actions.label: Attempt removal to trigger warning
actions.exact_action: Initiate the removal action in Geek and observe the resulting warning behavior.

stop_or_escalate_if: If removal is possible without the expected credentials, stop and escalate.
If no warning appears when removal is initiated, stop and escalate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The removal action “will come with a warning.”

success_criteria: You confirm Geek uses username/password login for access.
You confirm your account is authorized for removal actions (operators do not have credentials; supervisors do).
When a removal action is initiated, a warning dialog is shown.
healthy_conditions: Geek requires login credentials for sensitive removal actions.
Removal initiation triggers a warning dialog.
failure_conditions: Removal actions can be performed without the expected credentials.
No warning dialog appears when removal is initiated.
escalation_guidance: If removal is possible without the expected credentials or if no warning appears, stop and escalate. The source does not provide further diagnostic steps beyond this observation.

screens_or_images.description: Training frame evidence for login gating and warning behavior for removal actions in Geek.

missing_details: The source does not provide the exact warning text or the specific UI location/label of the warning dialog.
The source does not provide step-by-step UI navigation for the specific removal action (e.g., exact button/menu names) beyond the general concept of initiating removal.
